about: Compiler bugs that the human has ruled on, kept so that each can be confirmed later:
re-run on a newer compiler, and reported upstream to modular/modular once the human
approves the draft. Each reproducer was run on the pinned compiler when it was added.
The decision log (decision-log.md) holds the reasoning; this file lists the bugs and
their state. Status values: unfiled, filed, confirmed, fixed-upstream, not-a-bug.

bugs.title: xs[i] = f(xs) stores into a stale element when f grows or shrinks xs
bugs.reproducer:
def bump(mut xs: List[Int]) -> Int:
    xs.append(7)
    return 5


def main():
    var xs: List[Int] = [1, 2]
    xs[0] = bump(xs)
    print(xs[0], len(xs))
bugs.compiler: accepts and prints `1 3`: it locates xs[0] before the call, the append reallocates, and the store of 5 is lost

bugs.title: a struct initialized field by field destroys a field that was never set
bugs.reproducer:
struct Res(Movable):
    var id: Int

    def __init__(out self, id: Int):
        self.id = id

    def __del__(deinit self):
        print("drop", self.id)


struct Two(Movable):
    var a: Res
    var b: Res

    def __init__(out self):
        self.a = Res(1)
        self.b = Res(2)


def main():
    var t: Two
    t.a = Res(1)
    print(t.a.id)
bugs.compiler: prints `1`, `drop 1`, `drop 0`: it runs the destructor of t.b, which was never initialized
bugs.model: destroys only the fields that were initialized: prints `1`, `drop 1`

bugs.title: @fieldwise_init fails inside a struct cycle through a List, where the hand-written initializer compiles
bugs.compiler: rejects: "invalid implicit move: unexpected keyword argument 'move'". With B's initializer written by hand as `def __init__(out self, var a: A): self.a = a^`, it compiles and prints `1`
bugs.model: accepts it, as it accepts the hand-written form, and prints `1`
